## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to design a practical, beginner-friendly CI/CD flow for serverless apps, including versioned Lambda deployments, aliases, and rollback mechanisms. It also touches SAM templates, buildspecs, and minimal IAM permissions necessary for deploy actions.

## Key Concepts

- AWS Lambda versioning and aliases for safe deployments
- AWS SAM deployment patterns and minimal template snippets
- CodeBuild buildspecs and unit testing integration
- IAM least-privilege roles for CodePipeline/CodeBuild deploy actions

## Code Example

```yaml
# SAM template snippet
Resources:
  MyFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: app.lambda_handler
      Runtime: python3.8
      CodeUri: .
      AutoPublishAlias: live
      DeploymentPreference:
        Type: Linear
        Alarms:
          - !Ref MyAlarm
```

```yaml
# Buildspec example
version: 0.2
phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      python: 3.8
  build:
    commands:
      - pytest -q
      - sam deploy --config-file samconfig.toml --no-confirm-changeset
artifacts:
  files:
    - '**/*'
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you add a manual approval before prod promotion?
- How would you monitor deployment health and automatically rollback if the API latency spikes?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your understanding of disaster recovery strategies, cross-region data replication, and automated failover workflows using managed AWS services.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-region disaster recovery with warm standby architecture
- Route 53 failover routing with health checks for automatic traffic steering
- DynamoDB Global Tables for multi-region data consistency
- CloudFormation modularization for DR resource deployment
- CodePipeline promotion and rollback strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CloudFormation for us-west-2 DR ECS and Route 53
Resources:
  DRCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-dr-cluster
      ClusterSettings:
        - Name: containerInsights
          Value: enabled

  DRTaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-api
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: api
          Image: !Ref DockerImage
          Essential: true
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 80

  DRService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      Cluster: !Ref DRCluster
      ServiceName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-api-service
      TaskDefinition: !Ref DRTaskDefinition
      DesiredCount: 2
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          Subnets: !Ref DRSubnets
          SecurityGroups: !Ref DRSecurityGroups

  PrimaryHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:
      HealthCheckConfig:
        Type: HTTP
        FullyQualifiedName: primary-api.example.com
        Port: 80
        ResourcePath: /health
        RequestInterval: 10
        FailureThreshold: 3

  FailoverRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      SetIdentifier: primary
      FailoverRecordSet:
        Type: PRIMARY
        HealthCheckId: !Ref PrimaryHealthCheck
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt PrimaryALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt PrimaryALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID

  SecondaryRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      SetIdentifier: dr
      FailoverRecordSet:
        Type: SECONDARY
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt DRALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt DRALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to create ephemeral, per-PR test environments with minimal IaC, DNS wiring, and cleanup, all in a beginner-friendly way. It touches CloudFormation, ECS/Fargate, ALB, Route 53, and automation hooks.

## Key Concepts

- PR-based ephemeral environments
- CloudFormation templates with parameters
- ECS Fargate and ALB setup
- Route 53 alias records for preview DNS
- Automatic cleanup on PR close and health gates

## Code Example

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Parameters:
  PRTag:
    Type: String
  ContainerImage:
    Type: String
  DomainName:
    Type: String
Resources:
  PreviewALB:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'preview-alb-${PRTag}'
      Scheme: internet-facing
      Type: application
  PreviewTargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
  PreviewListener:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref PreviewALB
      Port: 80
      DefaultActions:
        - Type: forward
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref PreviewTargetGroup
  PreviewDNSRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneName: !Sub '${DomainName}.'
      Name: !Sub 'preview-${PRTag}.${DomainName}'
      Type: A
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt PreviewALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt PreviewALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you tear down old preview environments safely to avoid resource leaks or rate limits?
- What IAM policies would you apply to the deployment role to enforce least privilege across per-PR stacks?
